first_impression.reaction: Googled 'crete wedding packages' with a couple of resort PDFs already downloaded. The intro says what I suspected: same name, different product. No sunset poetry, no 'book now' in the takeaways. I went to the FAQ first, then 'What's left out or charged on top', then the checklist. It names resorts and gives me their actual conditions: three-night minimums, 10 rooms for two nights, Municipal and Metropolis fees on top, 'informal marriage' certificates. That's what I came for. My niggles: the opening line on what packages 'usually' cover goes a bit further than the venue detail backs up, one Abaton line reads oddly, and the venue run-through is padded with honeymoon extras.

journey.quote: Two Crete wedding packages can carry the same name and share almost nothing on paper.
journey.reaction: Good. That's my problem in one line, and nobody's selling me anything yet.

journey.quote: Most bundle a ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a chosen space.
journey.reaction: I read every venue below and never saw a single hour limit. And Euphoria's first tier, Elxi, doesn't list a coordinator. You only get one on Pathos and Eros. A small thing, but it's the kind of generalisation I'd check, and here it doesn't quite hold.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before you pay any deposit.
journey.reaction: Takeaways with no booking link. The first ask comes after the evidence. That's the right order.

journey.section: Resort packages with a minimum stay
journey.quote: Its packages are valid with a minimum booking of 10 rooms for at least two nights, depending on guest numbers, and they do not include the accommodation itself.
journey.reaction: That's the catch that would blow my budget, stated plainly with the venue named. Proof, not promises.

journey.quote: It records an informal ceremony, not a legal marriage.
journey.reaction: Telling me the hotel certificate isn't a marriage is exactly the sort of thing a sales page would bury. Credit for saying it.

journey.quote: Abaton's packages are complete, and their items are not interchangeable.
journey.reaction: Two lines earlier Abaton lets you 'create your own' and has a menu of extras. Then this standalone line says the packages are fixed. Later I read almost the same words about Euphoria. Is this really Abaton's policy, or a copy-paste? I scrolled back to check.

journey.quote: Deluxe Dream includes welcome drinks of homemade lemonade and berry water, champagne and chocolate strawberries in the honeymoon suite, and an event coordinator present throughout the stay.
journey.reaction: Lemonade and strawberries don't help me compare a quote. The coordinator bit does. The venue run-through has a lot of this (fireworks, breakfast in bed), and I skimmed it.

journey.section: Are Crete wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: The phrase "all inclusive" on a Crete resort usually describes the holiday, not the wedding.
journey.reaction: That's a trap I'd have walked into. Backed by two named resorts. Useful.

journey.quote: Out of the Blue settles registry office fees inside its Civil and Orthodox packages, so the same question has two different answers on one island.
journey.reaction: Showing both sides with named venues. This is what makes a comparison guide worth reading.

journey.quote: Ask whether the space you want carries a fee, and whether the arch in the photographs is part of your package.
journey.reaction: Ha. Exactly the upsell I'm worried about. Going in the spreadsheet.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: A planner connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, but adds another party to brief and another agreement to read closely.
journey.reaction: The planner option gets a downside like the other two. On a planner's own website. That's the balance I look for.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: Deposits and cancellation. Ask what the deposit secures, whether it is refundable, when the balance is due and what happens if you postpone.
journey.reaction: Right question. But this is the one line in the checklist with no real Crete example behind it, where nearly every other section had one. I'd still have to go and dig.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says some countries ask you to prove there is no impediment to your marriage, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages.
journey.reaction: Dated, and it names the government source. I can check that in thirty seconds.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation whether you already hold quotes or are still shaping your shortlist.
journey.reaction: CTA after the evidence, fine. 'In writing' is the right promise. But three lines up you asked me who carries the exchange-rate risk, and now you quote in AUD. So who carries it with you? I'd ask on the call.

journey.quote: Rarely. A package covers what its list names.
journey.reaction: Straight answer first, named exclusions behind it. That's what an FAQ is for.

journey.quote: Some include the official fees and some do not. At Elounda SA, the Municipal and Metropolis fees are charged on top of the package rate.
journey.reaction: Says 'some include' but only gives me the one that doesn't. The body had Out of the Blue as the counter-example. Why drop it here, where I read first?

unanswered_questions: What deposit and cancellation terms do the Crete resorts named here actually set?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these Crete resorts, and does that affect which ones get recommended? (deferred business detail)
When the Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD, whose exchange rate is used and who carries the currency risk between deposit and balance? (deferred business detail)
Is the first consultation free, and what do I walk away with? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real Crete wedding with the actual breakdown I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: Most bundle a ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a chosen space.
turn_offs_found.why: It's the opening claim, and the page never shows a venue limiting hours, and Euphoria's entry tier has no coordinator. Everything else is carefully pinned to named venues, so a sweeping 'most' that the detail doesn't bear out stands out. Mild, but it's the first thing I'd test.

turn_offs_found.quote: or return to our curated Greece wedding collection.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Curated' is marketing talk in the last line of an otherwise factual page. It doesn't tell me curated by whom or on what basis. Very mild, and it's the only one I found.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the quote checklist, to send to the two Crete resorts we're looking at
My parents, the legal side and the 'Australian couples' questions

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation whether you already hold quotes or are still shaping your shortlist.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned the ask. It comes after the evidence, the planner option got an honest downside, and 'in writing' is the right promise. What stops a straight yes is the question I ask every planner: do you take a cut from the venue, and is there a margin in the AUD quote? I'd want that answered before or on the first call.

top_3_changes: Bring the intro and first takeaway in line with the venue detail: 'a ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a space' is broader than what the page shows (no hour limits are named, and Euphoria's Elxi has no coordinator). Narrow it to what the named packages actually share.

Fix the standalone Abaton line 'Abaton's packages are complete, and their items are not interchangeable.' It sits right after Abaton's 'create your own' and its menu of extras, and almost repeats the Euphoria wording later. Either explain how the two fit or cut it.

In the FAQ 'Does a venue package include the legal paperwork?', add the Out of the Blue counter-example from the body so 'some include' is actually shown. (Commission, fee model and AUD margin would help me enquire, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and exclusions first, tested generalisations, looked for catches, fee model and currency risk
No invented brand facts; commission, fee, AUD conversion and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions and marked deferred
VERIFY marker and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA marker) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

open_questions.question: The intro's 'a coordinator and set hours' generalisation is not borne out by the venue detail. Is that a copy fix this round, or does the editor have evidence for it?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'crete wedding packages' with resort PDFs in hand, hence top relevance.
No prices on the page is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
